title: Introduce Minimal Input Stability Smokehook and CI adapter
author: Aditi Rao
body:
Context and motivation: We frequently see surface regressions that only manifest for extremely short/terse inputs (one- to three-token queries) — these failures are noisy in downstream apps (unexpected completions, prompt-parsing variance, tokenization edge-cases). This PR introduces a targeted smokehook that runs a compact, curated minimal-input prompt set during CI and on gated rollouts to detect brittleness in low-context behavior. The smokehook computes a compact 'stability score' from repeatability, tokenization-consistency, and normalized answer-surface similarity; failing scores trigger a soft-fail that quarantines the rollout and creates an actionable report.

What this change does (summary): adds a new smoke CI hook (MinimalInputStabilityHook) implemented in eval-harness/hooks, a small canonical minimal-input prompt corpus and associated golden-exemplar baselines, a CI job shape and runner that can be included as an optional pre-merge smoke check, and a lightweight reporter that outputs a machine-readable remediation suggestion (decode-mode change, increase min-length sampling, or fallback variant routing). The hook is intentionally conservative — it signals risk with a severity tag and does not block merges by default, but it is wired into canary rollouts to halt automated rollout promotion on repeated high-severity hits.

Checklist (author):
- [x] Implement hook logic and scoring functions (repeatability, tokenization variance, answer-surface similarity)
- [x] Add minimal-input prompt corpus and golden answers
- [x] Add unit tests for scoring edge cases and tokenization fuzz
- [x] Add CI job manifest and docs for enabling the smokehook
- [x] Wire reporter to produce JSON remediation hints for downstream runbooks
- [x] Add integration test for canary gating path

Files touched (high-level):
- eval-harness/hooks/minimal_input_stability_hook.py (core hook and score computation)
- eval-harness/tests/test_minimal_stability.py (unit + integration smoke tests)
- eval-harness/data/minimal_inputs/canonical_samples.yaml (prompt corpus)
- eval-harness/data/minimal_inputs/golden_baselines.json (golden outputs and matching rules)
- ci/jobs/eval-minimal-smokejob.yaml (optional CI job)
- docs/eval/minimal-input-stability.md (design and tuning guide)
- reporter/emitters/minimal_input_reporter.py (JSON remediation hints)
- examples/prompts/minimal_inputs.json (example usages for SDK quickstart)

Commits (summary):
- 9a3d7f0: initial scaffold for MinimalInputStabilityHook, scoring skeleton and config knobs
- b7f2c1a: add canonical prompt corpus and golden baseline artifacts; add matching rules
- d4e6ab3: unit tests for tokenizer-fuzz and repeatability; add CI job manifest
- f1c9b22: reporter that emits remediation hints; docs and examples; wire into smoke pipeline

Behavior and design notes (single-string): The hook runs N repeats (configurable, default 6) for each minimal prompt with deterministic seeds to measure repeatability; a tokenization-consistency pass checks off-by-one or subtoken splits that commonly cause different decoders to misalign; answer-surface similarity is computed via normalized BLEU-lite + lexical overlap and a small semantic-similarity fallback (sparse embedding cosine) for longer minimal outputs. The final stability score is in the interval [0,100]; thresholds are configurable per-repo and per-rollout stage. By default the CI job treats a score < 50 as a 'soft-fail' (annotated but non-blocking), while canary promotion will halt on two consecutive 'high' events (score < 30). The goal is to flag regressions early without creating noisier failures in everyday PRs.

Backward compatibility: The hook is opt-in in CI pipeline manifests and feature gated via eval-harness config; no existing gates are changed. The reporter's JSON schema is additive and does not alter existing reporters.

Operational/playbook: docs/eval/minimal-input-stability.md contains guidance: tuning thresholds for different model families, suggested mitigation steps (switch to sampling params, fallback to longer-context variant, pin quantization profile), and an incident template for triage that includes tokenization diffs and sample traces. The CI job has a 'quick' mode that runs a 12-sample fast pass and a 'full' mode that runs the canonical 120-sample suite.
review_comments: Jordan Kim: Nice scoped change. Two asks: (1) make the repeat count and seed deterministic via a shared util so other hooks can reuse it; (2) the tokenization diagnostics should include a byte-offset map in the JSON reporter so SRE can quickly map token splits to user strings.
Author (Aditi): Addressed — extracted stable-run util into eval-harness/util/stable_runner.py and added byte-offset token map to reporter output. PTAL.
Priya Patel: Tests look good but add a case where a model returns a prefixed whitespace-only token that changes normalization; we should ensure normalization rules are explicit in docs.
Author (Aditi): Added normalization unit and updated docs with explicit whitespace-normalization rules and example diffs.
Liam O'Connor: CI job looks fine; please add a comment about cost implication and a quick-mode default to limit runner minutes in PRs.
Author (Aditi): Added quick-mode and documented cost; CI was updated to run quick-mode in PRs and full-mode on nightly canaries.
Jordan Kim: Approving via GitHub review after final CI pass.
merge_commit_message: Introduce MinimalInputStabilitySmokehook: add hook, corpus, CI job, reporter, and docs
merge_outcome_notes: Merged after CI rerun fixed a flaky tokenization unit test; feature is behind opt-in flag and does not change existing gates.
release_notes: Add optional minimal-input stability smoke check and CI adapter (opt-in). Provides early detection for regressions on one- to three-token queries; includes remediation hints and canary gating integration.
extra_ci_details: Initial CI run failed due to nondeterministic tokenizer fixture; rerun succeeded after fixing seed in stable_runner util. Coverage: unit tests + small integration smoke pass. Checks: lint (pass), unit-tests (pass after rerun), integration-smoke (pass quick-mode), docs build (pass).
note_for_ops: When enabling in production canaries, start with threshold 30 and quick-mode nightly; escalate to 50 only after validating false-positive rate on a 7-day sliding window.
